about: Every source Roast Coach draws on, and what each one is good for. The app reads this file at startup; adding a source is dropping a file in and adding an entry here, not editing code.

sources.title: Modulating the Flavor Profile of Coffee: One Roaster's Manifesto
sources.author: Rob Hoos
sources.strongest: Maillard time — colour change to first crack — moves body and complexity. Four coffees, blind cupping panel, other segments held to within ten seconds, corroborated by thirteen logged production runs.
sources.rights: Copyright the author. This library holds findings and citations in our own words, not the book's text.

sources.title: Roasting Foundation
sources.author: Morten Münchow
sources.strongest: Colour accounts for roughly 80% of sensory variation and timing roughly 20%, from Giacalone, Münchow et al. (2018) in Food Quality and Preference — the only peer-reviewed result any of these sources rests a number on.
sources.rights: Copyright CoffeeMind. Findings and citations in our own words.

sources.title: The Coffee Roaster's Handbook: A How-To Guide for Home and Professional Roasters
sources.author: Len Brault
sources.strongest: A named roast-level ladder with temperatures, and a green-versus-roast fault test: run the same profile on another origin — if the fault does not follow, it came in with the bean.
sources.rights: Copyright the author. Findings and citations in our own words.
sources.caveat: The supplied copy has empty chapters from the cupping section onward, so nothing here rests on those.

sources.title: The Coffee Fermentation Flavor Continuum
sources.author: Chris Kornman
sources.strongest: Uniformity across the cups, not intensity in one, is what separates a successful ferment from the ferment defect.
sources.rights: Copyright Royal Coffee. Findings and citations in our own words.
sources.caveat: Appeals to research four times and names no study.

sources.title: Sensory Lexicon
sources.author: World Coffee Research
sources.strongest: 109 flavour attributes in 17 categories, each anchored to a physical reference standard and an absolute 0–15 intensity, so 'hazelnut 3.5' means the same thing in two roasteries.
sources.rights: Copyright © 2017 World Coffee Research. All rights reserved. This repository carries the attribute names, categories and reference intensities — which are facts — and not WCR's definitions. See the note in the file, and tools/import_lexicon.py.

sources.title: Arabica and Robusta Varieties Catalog
sources.author: World Coffee Research
sources.strongest: 117 varieties with lineage, genetic group, stature, bean size, optimal altitude by latitude, disease resistance and quality potential — the difference between a bean record that says 'Bourbon' and one that means something.
